summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass complicated by chronic post-bypass hypoglycemia requiring gastrostomy tube feeds was admitted to the bariatric surgery service for frequent reported hypoglycemic episodes associated with confusion and short-term memory loss, along with severe constipation, nausea/dry heaving, and recurrent epigastric pain. Neurology evaluated her and felt no additional imaging was needed, with symptoms most consistent with hypoglycemia-related episodes. Endocrinology supervised a daytime tube-feed hold with frequent glucose monitoring and planned critical labs if glucose fell below 55 mg/dL, but fingersticks remained above threshold throughout the stay; her home glucose meter was replaced due to discrepant readings. Gastroenterology performed an EGD showing abnormal mucosa in the esophagus and stomach with intact Roux-en-Y anatomy and no ulcer at the gastrojejunal anastomosis; metronidazole was stopped and antiemetic therapy was changed from ondansetron to prochlorperazine. She was discharged home ambulatory and mentally clear with a plan for nocturnal tube feeds (11 pm–7 am at 40) plus a complex-carbohydrate diet and outpatient follow-up in three weeks.
